title: Whole genome sequence of Bacillus licheniformis strain B65 recovered from the surface of a dairy pasteurizer after cleaning and disinfection
author: Instituut voor Landbouw en Visserijonderzoek
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0
materials: Whole genome sequence of Bacillus licheniformis strain B65 recovered from the surface of a dairy pasteurizer following cleaning and disinfection in the FASTA format. The bacteria was grown overnight in BHI broth and its DNA was extracted using the Qiagen tissue culture DNA extraction kit (DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kits). The genomic DNA was randomly sheared into short fragments. The obtained fragments were end repaired, A-tailed and further ligated with Illumina adapter. The library was checked with Qubit and real-time PCR for quantification and bioanalyzer for size distribution detection. Quantified libraries were pooled and sequenced on Illumina platform (NovaSeq

steps.title: Overnight bacterial culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate Bacillus licheniformis strain B65 into BHI broth and incubate overnight at the appropriate temperature.

steps.title: Genomic DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from the overnight culture using the Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (catalogue DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kits) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: DNA fragmentation
steps.instruction: Randomly shear the extracted genomic DNA into short fragments.

steps.title: End‑repair, A‑tailing, adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Perform end‑repair and A‑tailing of the fragmented DNA, then ligate Illumina sequencing adapters to the A‑tailed fragments.

steps.title: Library quality control
steps.instruction: Quantify the library with Qubit and real‑time PCR, and assess fragment size distribution using a Bioanalyzer.

steps.title: Library pooling and sequencing
steps.instruction: Pool the quantified libraries and sequence them on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, adjusting the pool according to effective library concentration and the required data amount.

steps.title: Read cleaning
steps.instruction: Clean the raw sequencing reads using the Clean Data pipeline (or equivalent cleaning procedure).

steps.title: SOAPdenovo assembly
steps.instruction: Assemble the cleaned reads with SOAPdenovo using K‑mers 95, 107, and 119; evaluate each assembly and select the K‑mer that yields the fewest scaffolds as the optimal assembly.

substeps.instruction: Compare scaffold counts and choose the optimal K‑mer

steps.title: SPAdes assembly
steps.instruction: Assemble the reads with SPAdes using the default K‑mers of 99 and 127, then choose the assembly that produces the minimal number of scaffolds.

substeps.instruction: Select the assembly with the fewest scaffolds

steps.title: Abyss assembly
steps.instruction: Assemble the reads with Abyss using a K‑mer of 64.

steps.title: Integrate assemblies with CISA
steps.instruction: Combine the SOAPdenovo, SPAdes, and Abyss assemblies using CISA software and retain the integrated result that has the least scaffolds.

steps.title: Gap filling
steps.instruction: Use GapClose software to fill gaps in the integrated preliminary assembly.

steps.title: Depth and length filtering
steps.instruction: Remove reads whose sequencing depth is lower than 0.35 × the average depth and discard fragments shorter than 500 bp.

substeps.instruction: Filter out low‑depth reads (<0.35 × average depth)

steps.title: Finalize assembly for annotation
steps.instruction: Prepare the filtered, gap‑closed assembly for gene prediction; overall genome coverage should be >99 %.
